claim: Lakatos names a closed menu of responses to a counterexample (surrender, monster-barring, exception-barring, monster-adjusting, lemma-incorporation) and splits failures into local (a proof step) and global (the claim). Only lemma-incorporation and monster-adjusting improve the claim; the barring moves protect it.
agent_test: Label each revision in a conjecture task by move type (code-checked by re-running all earlier cases); compare accuracy when barring moves are blocked vs allowed, equal tokens.

claim: A revision that redefines a term to exclude a counterexample can silently save a false claim; the program must demand an explicit new definition and re-test all earlier cases.
agent_test: Seed tasks with a known counterexample; count runs that rescue the claim by redefinition with vs without the re-test rule.

claim: Human problem-posing interventions show large pooled gains (Hedges g about 0.64-1.31), but with high heterogeneity, quasi-experimental designs, researcher-made tests and a null achievement result in a small trial; the true effect is likely much smaller.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent directly; use only as a prior. Test posing-before-solving instead (K18).
gap_search_note: Zhang 2024: g=0.72 [0.53,0.90], I2=69.2%, controlled designs smaller (58%), Egger significant; outcome is posing skill, not solving. Stays contested.

claim: What-If-Not itself is barely tested: the only opened WIN-specific study (N=68, two intact classes) bundles it with a scientific-approach lesson and measures posing ability, not solving. No LLM study tests an attribute-list-and-negate procedure.
agent_test: Build a WIN operator (list givens, negate each, solve variants, compare); test against plain restate-and-vary and no-variant at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Zhang 2024 lists what-if-not only as one strategy component; no WIN-only effect. Still single-source.

claim: Posing problems at the edge of the solver ability gives denser training signal than attempting unproved targets (STP: 28.5% vs 13.2% on LeanWorkbook; 131 correct of 2.5M proofs on unproved statements vs at least 47% of conjectures proved). This is a weight-training result; Minimo shows the same difficulty-targeting in small axiom domains.
agent_test: At inference, generate sub-lemmas, keep those the solver proves at pass rate in (0, 1/4] across K samples, and compare final accuracy with solving the target directly at equal tokens.

claim: Self-posing loops drift toward easy, trivial or topic-narrow statements unless code corrects it (Minimo hindsight ablation; STP mode collapse, fixed by a must-use-seed-lemma rule and Wasserstein reweighting; LeanConjecturer context effect).
agent_test: Run a posing loop with and without a code triviality and spread filter; report fraction trivial and distinct-topic count at equal tokens.

claim: Raw model conjecture output has low yield after code filters: about 31% novel and non-trivial (LeanConjecturer, 3,776 of 12,289); 9.5% of unique group-theory conjectures survive testing (40 of 420; 27% of the 149 that were testable); 3-6% of stated answers match the gold in ConjectureBench.
agent_test: Budget posing at 3-10x the number of survivors needed; measure survivors per 1k tokens.

claim: Running code to search for counterexamples prunes most model conjectures and can settle open ones; an attempted disproof also reveals misstated claims (Erdos #125, #741(i) amended).
agent_test: On conjecture tasks, require a code counterexample search before any proof; compare with model-judged truth at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Code search prunes and finds counterexamples, but REFUTE shows <9% falsification of subtly wrong code even with execution; gain depends on correct brute-force code. Narrowed, not weakened: status stays established for pruning, contested for accuracy gain.

claim: Separating conjecturing from proving and keeping verified results in context found a hard target theorem in 5/20 runs vs 0/20 for joint generation (Fisher p=0.024, one theorem, o3, topology).
agent_test: Run a pose-then-prove loop with a verified-lemma log vs single-pass solve on a set of lemma-rich tasks at equal tokens; use more than one target.

claim: Showing earlier verified theorems in context raises later proof success (99% vs 91% re-proof; target 7/80 vs 0/80), even when they are not used as lemmas; caveat is that the same model made them.
agent_test: Ablate the verified-findings log (present vs absent) on related-problem sequences.
gap_search_note: Prover Agent and 2606.28747 show verified lemmas in context help in formal settings; still no second-target replication of CPL 5/20 vs 0/20.

claim: Stating the target conjecture or answer is a separate and weak skill: standalone equiv-rfl pass@1 is 3.3-3.7%, and end-to-end autoformalisation falls by an average 23.7% when the answer is hidden. The 78.77 to 26.70 ConJudge pair mixes seen/unseen with a few-shot ablation and must not be read as the pure answer-leak effect.
agent_test: Score a separate explicit conjecture slot before solving, with answer-leak vs hidden-answer variants.
gap_search_note: DAP: LLMs exceed 80% answer accuracy on PutnamBench where formal provers get under 10%; answer discovery in natural language is NOT weak. K11 holds only for stating the target in formal form (equiv-rfl).

claim: Gains from the LEAN-FIRE conjecturing prompt came from few-shot examples, not the reasoning structure.
agent_test: Compare examples-only vs structure-only prompts at equal tokens.

claim: More agent machinery did not help on open conjectures: literature access (476,000 papers) and a sub-agent/memory loop gave no gain; solve rate rose about 10 points per tenfold spend. A basic generate-and-verify agent also replicated AlphaProof Nexus on Erdos problems but cost more on the hardest.
agent_test: Compare a bare verify loop against the full scaffold at matched spend.

claim: LLMs judge truth of conjectures poorly in both directions: they write proofs of false statements (best model 29.0% sycophantic; up to 15.6 points worse on their own posed flaw) and they wrongly call a true theorem false (GPT-4o 10 of 16 natural-language trials; o3 always).
agent_test: Replace model-judged validity with code check; measure error both ways on seeded true/false claims.

claim: A fixed validate-first instruction partly reduces sycophancy (DeepSeek-V3.1 +34.1%, direction of the number is ambiguous in the text); best-of-n, confidence selection and fine-tuning help little.
agent_test: Compare validate-first, code-check, and neither on seeded false claims.

claim: Authoring hard valid problems is a different skill from solving; the best author was not the best solver, newcomer models author problems that defeat prior top solvers 27.6% vs 8.0%.
agent_test: Measure whether the agent self-posed variants are valid and discriminating, independent of its solve rate.
gap_search_note: Code2Math: 74/90 to 98/98 internally accepted variants certified by external judge; strong generators exist but need a second check.

claim: Pushing a model to pose harder problems raises invalid or wrong-key rate (5.1% to 25.0% over three stages) and a validity gate removes about 2% of items; code execution at solve time helps only a little.
agent_test: Gate every posed variant by an independent check before use; log rejection rate.
gap_search_note: Consistent: self-check alone lets 0-18% of variants through as ill-posed.

claim: Rewriting a problem conditions to harder variants cuts accuracy by an average 21.73% across 26 models, so condition-change variants expose memorised solution forms; rule-based swaps can make items ill-posed.
agent_test: Solve a problem plus its what-if-not variants; flag answers that stay unchanged when the conditions change.

claim: Most unexpected human-posed responses come from misreading the task (74% task understanding, 18% connection, 8% generation), so a restatement step precedes posing.
agent_test: Compare restate-then-pose with direct pose on ill-posed output rate.

claim: Resampling one model yields repeated conjectures: 55.5% unique, cosine self-similarity 0.25-0.42, and more trials did not help; structured operators are needed for diversity.
agent_test: Compare distinct-variant counts for resampling vs operator-driven variation at equal tokens.

claim: Self-posed conjecture training helps the poser own domain but transfer is doubtful: LeanConjecturer GRPO moved solved problems 47 to 50 of 192 and 9/14 to 8/14 on the held-out set, while STP reports 2-3% on external benchmarks.
agent_test: Not applicable to a no-training agent; note only.
gap_search_note: Code2Math SFT +4.5/+4.7 AIME points and CounterMATH SFT AIME24 20.0 to 30.0 (3 problems) are training results with one run; transfer remains contested.

claim: Building the explicit counterexample or construction is the hard half of refutation (ALPS: 0 on construction side; 64.5% of group-theory test code did not run).
agent_test: Measure counterexample-search success when a code sandbox is available vs not.
gap_search_note: REFUTE and CounterMATH add independent support: constructing the counterexample is hard.

claim: Strong falsification skill does not follow from strong solving skill: o3-mini (high) solves about 48.7% of REFUTE problems from scratch but breaks under 9% of wrong solutions; most failed search runs come from wrong brute-force code (86% of failed RandSearch runs).
agent_test: Run the check code on tiny known-true and known-false cases before trusting a no-counterexample result; compare false-pass rate with and without that gate.

claim: Small-cases-then-generalize beats pure brute force on construction tasks (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 19.2% vs 9.9%; GPT-4o 12.9% vs 7.6%), and a Python interpreter roughly doubles accuracy at about 5x cost, from a low base.
agent_test: Compare compute-small-cases-then-conjecture with direct proof at equal tokens on pattern-finding problems; run with and without a code sandbox.

claim: Hiding the target answer is a large, real difficulty change and leaving it visible invites cheating: LLMs exceed 80% answer accuracy on PutnamBench while formal provers get under 10%; spurious rfl proofs appear when the answer is in the statement.
agent_test: Run the same items with the answer hidden vs stated; count spurious or circular solutions; keep items with leaked targets out of scoring.

claim: A solver's own what-if-not or evolved variants are sometimes ill-posed even after a self-check (up to 18% rejected by an external judge in Code2Math; MathDuels error rates 5.1 to 25.0%); an independent check is needed.
agent_test: Measure the ill-posed rate of generated variants with a same-model check vs an independent model check.

claim: Auxiliary lemmas that are special cases of the target matter as much as subgoals: in Prover Agent, 25% of used lemmas were special cases and 25% technique-inducing vs 41.7% subgoals (small sample).
agent_test: Add a specialize-first step (small cases of the claim) and compare against a subgoal-only step at equal tokens.

claim: Human problem-posing meta-analysis updated: g=0.72 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.90) for posing skill, I2 69%, pre-post designs about 58% larger than controlled ones, asymmetric funnel; no study isolates What-If-Not, and the outcome is not solving accuracy.
agent_test: Not applicable; use only as caution that human posing gains do not transfer to an LLM scaffold.
